A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Value Residual Learning and its ResFormer/SVFormer architectures. All main-text and appendix pages are readable, and corresponding text, equations, figures, and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v4 reports original language-model training results, architectural ablations, attention analyses, and downstream reasoning scores, including Tables 2 and 11.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical analyses and reports additional variant, scaling, and downstream results in Figure 2 and Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: v5 Section 3.2 adds Learnable ResFormer Plus, initializing first-layer value coefficients through cross-layer softmax normalization with a shared scale initialized to the layer count. This extends the coefficient-learning approach while retaining the underlying ResFormer and SVFormer attention procedures.

E1.justification: v5 adds WikiText language modeling, LAMBADA prediction, and BoolQ question answering alongside the six retained reasoning benchmarks. The new scaling experiment uses internal pretraining data, but its unspecified composition does not establish additional domain or language coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 2 expands the central scaling comparisons from a vanilla Transformer baseline to include NeuTRENO and DenseFormer. These methods also join the downstream comparison in v5 Table 2; v4 evaluated them in its 82M comparison but not its scaling or downstream comparisons. This substantially broadens direct evaluation against related residual methods.

E3.justification: Beyond the retained 82M–468M/20B-token study, v5 adds a 1.6B/200B-token protocol using 8,192-token sequences, a 1.5e-4 learning rate, and evaluation every 10B tokens. Downstream reporting adds perplexity and an eight-task accuracy average. Separately, v4 Table 2/v5 Table 3 revise two Constant/Sparse configurations from 0.5Vn to Vn while retaining their losses; this does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v5 Table 3 extends the variant analysis to test Plus weighting/initialization against standard learnable and manually configured residuals. Existing learning-rate controls, residual-source/type ablations, module-removal analyses, PCA, and appendix attention-pattern and rescaling studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v5's GPU-hours-per-run disclosure concerns computational cost, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 2 adds comparator, Plus, and 1.6B scaling results; reported parameter/data savings change from 13.3%/15.4% to 16.11%/20.3%. Table 3 adds Plus loss 2.681. New Table 2 reports downstream averages of 42.3 for Learnable ResFormer and 40.6 for Transformer, replacing v4 Table 11's two-length results. The downstream scores are not directly comparable across versions because their reported settings and task averages differ.

T1.justification: v5 adds the mathematical definition of Plus coefficients using normalized exponentials and a shared scale in Section 3.2. Existing appendix entropy definitions and mathematical analyses remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the quantified efficiency claim from 13.3% fewer parameters and 15.4% less data to 16.11% and 20.3%. The central contributions concerning first-layer value residuals and approximately halved SVFormer KV cache remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations involving initial-information dilution, attention-sink disruption, and SVFormer's sequence-length and learning-rate dependence remain substantively unchanged. The limitations about imperfect coefficient learning and unavailable larger-scale validation are also retained, despite the added scaling experiment.

D1.justification: v5 supplies settings and approximately 3,584 H800 GPU hours per run for the new 1.6B experiment, but does not specify the internal corpus's composition or access. Conversely, v5 Table 9 omits the 82M Llama and 78M GPT2 size labels supplied in v4 Table 8. Existing appendix training-detail tables are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work discussion remain unchanged. Positioning relative to DenseFormer, NeuTRENO, and KV-sharing methods, including the claimed novelty of decoupling values, is retained.

P1.justification: v5 combines baseline preliminaries, merges scaling and residual-method comparisons, and integrates downstream evaluation into the main text. It also makes localized language and indexing corrections and adds an affiliation and acknowledgments. Most narrative and appendix explanations remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 revises indexing and the NeuTRENO schematic. Figure 2 becomes a full-width, three-panel display with additional curves, and a new main-text downstream table replaces v4's appendix table. Several retained tables are reformatted or repositioned, while Figures 3–15 retain their underlying graphical content.

improvement.justification: Expanded comparisons against NeuTRENO and DenseFormer, broader downstream evaluation, and the 1.6B/200B-token experiment strengthen empirical support beyond v4's smaller-scale training tests. The improvement is limited by insufficient documentation of the internal corpus, removal of sequence-length-specific downstream results, and the unrevised larger-scale-validation limitation. These shortcomings temper the added evidence without outweighing it.
